name: Copley Press, Inc. v. Superior Court
summary: Copley Press sought access to records of disciplinary proceedings against police officers. The California Supreme Court held that pre-SB 1421 (2018), peace officer personnel records — including discipline records — were categorically confidential under Penal Code § 832.7 and the CPRA § 6254(c) personnel file exemption (now § 7923.625). SB 1421 subsequently overruled this holding for specified categories of records.
holding: Prior to SB 1421 (2018), Penal Code § 832.7 created a categorical confidentiality rule for peace officer personnel records, including discipline files, that superseded the CPRA's general public-interest balancing test. Records of Internal Affairs investigations were confidential absent a court order. NOTE: SB 1421 (effective January 1, 2019) substantially overruled this holding by making specified categories of officer misconduct records public under Penal Code § 832.7.

legal_definitions.term: peace officer personnel records — pre-SB 1421 rule
legal_definitions.definition: Under the pre-2019 regime, peace officer personnel records were categorically confidential under Pen. Code § 832.7, shielding discipline, complaints, and Internal Affairs records from CPRA disclosure without a court order or statutory exception.
legal_definitions.context: This rule was fundamentally altered by SB 1421 (2018), which made records of use of force, sexual assault, and dishonesty findings publicly disclosable.
legal_definitions.notes: Partially overruled by SB 1421 (2018) effective January 1, 2019

relevance_to_audit: Critical for CPRA audits involving law enforcement records requests. Post-SB 1421 (2019), the categorical confidentiality rule no longer applies to use-of-force records, sexual assault findings, and dishonesty findings under Pen. Code § 832.7. Agencies that continue to invoke § 7923.625 to shield all officer records without SB 1421 analysis are misapplying the exemption.

key_quotes.text: Penal Code section 832.7 creates a broad, categorical rule of confidentiality for peace officer personnel records that was intended to supersede the balancing test otherwise available under Government Code section 6255.
key_quotes.context: Describing the pre-SB 1421 rule; substantially abrogated by legislation effective January 1, 2019.

procedural_posture: Writ of mandate to compel disclosure; denied
subsequent_treatment: Partially overruled by SB 1421 (Stats. 2018, ch. 988) which created public right of access to specified peace officer misconduct records effective January 1, 2019
